title: Propagate Allow/Disallow Labels on a DAG
description_html:
You are given a directed acyclic graph G(V, E). Each node v has two sets of lowercase letters: Allow(v) and Disallow(v). Constraints are transitive along paths: if there is a path from u to v, then u's allow/disallow affect v.

For each node v, accumulate over all ancestors x of v (including v itself):

  • A(v) = ⋃ Allow(x)
  • D(v) = ⋃ Disallow(x)

The effective allowed set is Effective(v) = A(v) \ D(v) (a letter disallowed by ANY ancestor is excluded, even if some ancestor allowed it).

Input

  • First line: n m (#nodes, #edges).
  • Next n lines: allow_i disallow_i (lowercase a–z; - means empty).
  • Next m lines: u v meaning u → v (1-indexed), guaranteed acyclic.

Output

n lines; line i is Effective(i) in sorted order, or - if empty.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5, 0 ≤ m ≤ 2·10^5; alphabet fixed at 26.

Example

3 2
a -
- b
c -
1 2
2 3
----
a
a
ac

See Notes for the approach (topological-order bitmask propagation), the follow-up trio, and related problems.
